facts.text: A Gantt chart represents tasks as horizontal calendar bars from start to finish; a milestone is a dated event with no duration; a dependency specifies that one task cannot start until another finishes.
facts.quote: A Gantt chart is a calendar drawing in which each task is a horizontal bar from its start to its finish, a milestone is a single dated event with no duration, and a dependency is the rule that one task cannot start until another has finished.

facts.text: The Gantt chart is named after engineer Henry Gantt, who popularized the chart in the early 1900s.
facts.quote: named after the engineer Henry Gantt, who popularized it in the early 1900s.

facts.text: In the collision-mitigation validation program, sensor-model correlation cannot start until a sensor has been chosen and real recordings exist.

facts.text: In the collision-mitigation validation program, the hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) bench cannot be finished until the control unit's interfaces are stable.

facts.text: Chapter 12 recommends drawing validation plans with time horizontally and evidence streams vertically, showing dependencies and gate diamonds rather than isolated boxes.
facts.quote: Put time horizontally and evidence streams vertically, with dependencies and gate diamonds rather than isolated boxes.

facts.text: Chapter 12 considers a roadmap without gate criteria, evidence ownership or schedule logic merely a picture rather than an adequate plan.
facts.quote: A roadmap without gate criteria, evidence ownership or schedule logic "is a picture".

facts.text: When several parallel task paths converge on a milestone, a single-date plan is optimistic because of merge bias: if three tasks must finish before a fourth starts, the probability that all three finish on time is lower than the probability for any one task.
facts.quote: an effect known as merge bias: if three tasks must all finish before a fourth starts, the chance that all three are on time is lower than the chance for any one.

facts.text: Chapter 12 recommends integration before optimization, exercising the whole validation chain early even with crude components.

facts.text: Chapter 12 identifies late integration as a repeatedly documented cause of failure.

facts.text: Hardware arrival fixes the validation program's deadline, making the chains of dependent tasks ending at that date the important scheduling concern.
